title: Minimum Moves to Get a Peaceful Board
summary: Given an n x n chess board with rooks placed at rooks[i] = [xi, yi], find the minimum moves needed to ensure each row and column contains exactly one rook.
statement: Given an n x n chess board with rooks placed at rooks[i] = [xi, yi], find the minimum moves needed to ensure each row and column contains exactly one rook. Moves are vertical or horizontal to adjacent cells, and no two rooks can occupy the same cell during the process.
constraints: There are n distinct rook cells on an n by n board with zero-based coordinates.
One move shifts one rook one cell horizontally or vertically; finish with exactly one rook per row and per column.
Return the minimum number of moves; a collision-free order of the moves is guaranteed to exist.
hints: Vertical and horizontal costs are independent, reducing the board problem to two one-dimensional assignments.
Sort row coordinates and match them to target rows 0..n-1; do the same for columns.
The uncrossing exchange argument makes sorted matching optimal in one dimension, and independent coordinate moves let the two minima add.
editorial: The uncrossing exchange argument makes sorted matching optimal in one dimension, and independent coordinate moves let the two minima add.

tests.explanation: Sorted row targets cost one move and sorted column targets cost two, totaling three.
Each row and column already contains one rook, so zero moves are needed.
